Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2026-04-14 16:30 PDT
- Duration: 52m approx
- Attendees: Jamie (Redwood AE), Ria (Redwood SE), Alicia (ThermaCloud SRE), Markus (CTO), Dev (ML Eng), Priya (Product)

Optional Summary: (auto)
- Quick sync after last week's intermittent 502/timeouts during thermal event on their edge fleet. Focus: confirm root cause (thermal-induced instance CPU throttling + upstream rate-window mismatch), validate mitigation (adaptive retry + graceful degrade to compact model), and agree next steps for pilot extension.

Topics:
- Incident recap and observed signatures
- Telemetry gaps and log correlation strategy
- Short-term mitigations: retry/backoff, kv-cache priming, rate-window smoothing
- Longer-term: Dedicated capacity vs hosted fallback, on-prem thermal constraints and thermal-aware autoscaling
- Next steps and ownerships

--- Transcript body (timestamps approximate, ASR imperfect) ---
[00:00] Jamie: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'll kick off — quick goal for today is to close the triage on the spike from Sunday and align on the pilot steps. Ria's got the instrumentation notes.
[00:18] Alicia: Yeah thanks. Uh, really appreciate you fitting us in. The short version — Sunday evening we saw a 3x latency spike and a bunch of 502s, some clients dropped requests. We correlate it to a thermal event on a subset of our edge fleet, but we also saw request bursts from the mobile app that lined up.
[00:42] Ria: Quick clarifying Q — when you say thermal event, is that CPU throttling on the box or like GPU thermal?
[00:49] Alicia: It's CPU throttling on the inference nodes, they're CPU-only boxes for the compact model. We do have a few GPU spots but those are used for training. The ASR logs show increased p95, and some of the clients retried aggressively which actually amplified the pool.
[01:12] Markus: And to add, our edge autoscaler is reactive — it scales when CPU hits 70% for two consecutive minutes. The initial surge happened faster than the scale-up, so we had some queuing.
[01:26] Jamie: That matches what we saw in the pilot traces — a hot key surge, K V cache cold misses, and then time spent loading context. Also we see the gateway rate-windowing is narrow so when a bunch of clients retry you get a micro-burst.
[01:42] Dev: Note: some of the transcriptions earlier showed K V as K V cache and the model logs looked like KVCACHE flushes at the same time as throttles.
[01:54] Ria: Ok, so this is multi-factor: thermal causing per-node slowdown, cold KV cache making each request heavier, and client retry amplification due to aggressive client-side backoff absence.
[02:08] Priya: On product side we got a few user complaints, we need to know what's an acceptable SLA while we run the pilot.
[02:14] Jamie: Understood. We proposed a 99.5 p95 for the pilot, but given the thermal constraints we can discuss graceful degrade — i.e., route to compact model with shorter max tokens or early-stopping when latency budgets are tight.
[02:32] Alicia: Quick question: Does Redwood have any runtime thermal awareness? Like can it detect increased CPU scheduling latency and change behavior?
[02:41] Ria: We don't get OS-level temperature, but our runtime monitors token throughput and per-request service time. We can do adaptive throttling — reduce batch sizes, lower kv-cache pre-warm thresholds, or switch to a lower-cost model variant when tail latency exceeds a threshold. It's not exact thermal sensing but it reacts to observed slowdown.
[03:05] Markus: So that would be useful. We want an automated fallback to avoid mass client retries.
[03:11] Jamie: Right, and we can set a failover policy: when node p95 exceeds X ms for Y seconds, switch routing for new requests to dedicated region or compact model. We'll propose thresholds after the soak tests.
[03:24] Alicia: The confusing bit for us — the 502s were both at the gateway and at the model. Some of the 502s list internal errors that look like timeouts; others were upstream (our CDN) giving 502 on connection reset. So we need better correlation.
[03:41] Ria: We'll need request IDs and trace IDs across the stack. Could you share sample request IDs from Sunday?
[03:46] Alicia: Yeah, we'll pull them. ACTION: Alicia to dump the sample IDs — I'll attach in the ticket.
[03:52] Jamie: Perfect. Also, can you share the per-instance CPU scheduling logs? Even coarse metrics help.
[03:56] Alicia: Yep.
[04:01] --- ~5m pass, instrumentation discussion ~
[04:12] Ria: On mitigations we proposed three quick wins: 1) adaptive client retry guidance (increase jitter & cap retries), 2) enable KV cache priming on warmup for the top 20 request patterns, 3) implement graceful degrade to compact model with token cap.
[04:32] Dev: For KV priming, we'll need a list of the top patterns — I can generate that. It's about 60% of traffic hitting the same prompt templates.
[04:40] Ria: Great, that helps the warm-up ROI.
[04:43] Jamie: Also recommend smoothing gateway rate-windowing — widen the window to avoid micro-bursts, that fixed similar issues on another pilot.
[04:50] Markus: There's a tradeoff with perceived latency for single requests if you widen too much. We need to simulate.
[04:58] Ria: We can run a small synthetic load test that reproduces client retry patterns. We'll run two runs: one with current retry policy, one with capped exponential backoff, and measure tail.
[05:10] Alicia: Sounds good.
[05:12] --- ~Next: Adaptive retry soak and logs planning ~
[05:20] Ria: For the soak we'll put adaptive-retry on (client-side cap of 3 with jitter) and also enable warmup priming. We'll run 50k tokens over 2 hours — should be enough to warm caches.
[05:33] Dev: 50k tokens seems low — but for the compact model maybe ok. If you want realistic wear we can schedule a longer run over the weekend.
[05:42] Ria: Let's start small and escalate. If 50k shows improvement we'll do a longer weekend run.
[05:47] Priya: If the soak shows improvement, what does pilot success look like?
[05:52] Jamie: Pilot success criteria: 1) no unexplained 5xxs during a 24h window for the targeted routes, 2) p95 below agreed threshold (TBD), 3) KV cache hit rate improvement by 20%.
[06:05] Alicia: That sounds fair.
[06:08] --- ~Telemetry gaps and correlation ~
[06:12] Ria: We noticed some missing trace spans at the CDN handoff. If you can add trace injection at the edge for a subset of requests that will let us follow IDs end-to-end.
[06:22] Alicia: We can add trace injection, but that needs a small change to the edge script. We'll do it for 1% of traffic to start.
[06:29] Jamie: Perfect. Also, please include the response size and token count in the logs — those are helpful for kernel-level perf anomalies.
[06:41] Alicia: Noted.
[06:43] --- ~Customer: questions about Dedicated vs Hosted & security ~
[06:48] Markus: If we go Dedicated (reserved), do we get isolation from these thermal edge issues? I assume Dedicated pools are in a different infra region, but thermal is still possible if we use same instance types.
[07:00] Ria: Dedicated gives you capacity isolation and guaranteed pool size so you don't see noisy neighbor effects from other tenants. Thermal events on customer-managed hardware are still a thing; if you choose Redwood-managed Dedicated, we can choose instance types with better thermal headroom (bigger vCPU, or GPUs where applicable).
[07:18] Jamie: Also, Dedicated lets you pre-warm KV caches and have pinned model variants; that reduces cold-miss amplification.
[07:27] Markus: Ok. We also have questions about logs retention and audit for security, our SOC2 team will require the audit trail.
[07:34] Jamie: I'll share the security deck and SOC2 evidence link after this call. (Link placeholder: https://redwood.example/sd/security-deck)
[07:44] --- ~Mid call: root-cause hypotheses and experiment design ~
[07:50] Ria: Hypothesis A: thermal-triggered CPU slowdown + KV cold miss amplifies per-request CPU, causing gateway timeouts. Hypothesis B: client retry amplification is the root cause; thermal only exacerbates it. We propose experiments to isolate: 1) run client retry-capped test with warm KV, 2) run warm KV but aggressive retries, 3) run with graceful degrade enabled and observe 5xx reduction.
[08:18] Dev: For (1) we need the top-20 prompt prefixes, which I can provide by EOD.
[08:24] Alicia: We'll provide sample request IDs for Sunday incidents.
[08:28] Jamie: Good. We'll also instrument a Canary route that routes 5% of traffic to Redwood-hosted lower-latency zone to see if it reduces 5xxs — but we need permission to mirror that.
[08:41] Markus: We'd want to keep it minimal — 1-2% to start.
[08:45] Jamie: Fine.
[08:47] --- ~Crosstalk: small interruptions, ASR noise ~
[08:51] Unidentified Speaker: sorry, one sec — network flappin in our side —
[08:55] Alicia: that's fine, keep going.
[08:58] --- ~Tuning knobs discussed ~
[09:00] Ria: Tuning knobs we recommend: lower batch-size under high p95, cap concurrency per connection, aggressive kv prewarm for top templates, widen gateway rate-window, client-side retry guidance, and model-level early-stopping.
[09:18] Dev: For model early-stopping, how do you define a safe token cap? We can't break semantics.
[09:24] Ria: We use a confidence-based early stop for some tasks — if the model returns high confidence and the delta in tokens is small, we stop. For chat/longform it's trickier; we recommend content-based heuristics and always fall back to compact model rather than truncating in-place.
[09:40] Priya: We need to evaluate UX impact — we'll coordinate with your product folks.
[09:44] Jamie: We'll draft an impact matrix and share.
[09:48] --- ~Decision points and immediate plan ~
[09:50] Jamie: Immediate plan: run a 50k token adaptive soak with kv priming and capped retries. Ria will run tests and share logs. Customer will provide request IDs and top-20 patterns. We'll widen the gateway rate window in the staging environment and compare. If soak reduces 5xxs by 80%, we'll schedule a weekend 12-hour run.
[10:13] Alicia: We agree. Also please include timestamps on each log line — correlation is critical.
[10:19] Ria: We'll include full ms timestamps and trace IDs.
[10:22] Jamie: I'll pack the proposed thresholds into a small doc and send — p95 trigger, window seconds, fallback model id.
[10:30] --- ~Wrap up and next steps recap ~
[10:32] Jamie: Recap: Alicia dumps request IDs + CPU logs; Dev produces top-20 prompt prefixes; Ria runs soak and shares logs; Jamie sends pricing and security deck. Follow-up deep-dive scheduled tentative Tue 2026-04-20 (telemetry).
[10:46] Markus: One last ask — can you include a quick troubleshooting playbook we can hand to on-call to run during a surge?
[10:53] Ria: Yes, we'll include a short runbook (3 steps) and a checklist for failover.
[10:58] Alicia: Great. That should help cut time-to-detection.
[11:03] Jamie: Awesome, thanks everyone. We'll circulate notes and action items.
[11:08] End of meeting.
